# How on time are Island Transit's buses?

[Island Transit's buses send out their location every few seconds, but nobody
keeps those updates. This site saves every one, works out how often each bus
left its stops on time, and checks how trustworthy the tracking data is.
Everything is free to download.]{.lede}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
STATUS_URL = "https://ekczqlmunyumtgtthppb.supabase.co/rest/v1/status_now"
PUBLIC_KEY = "sb_publishable_AWlvBYVrlTz7dEaf7RwwzA_5zRN3af-"
status = {
  try {
    const r = await fetch(STATUS_URL, {headers: {apikey: PUBLIC_KEY}});
    return r.ok ? await r.json() : null;
  } catch (e) { return null; }
}
vp = status?.find(d => d.feed === "vehiclePositions") ?? null
ago = s => s < 120 ? `${s} seconds ago` : s < 7200 ? `${Math.round(s / 60)} minutes ago` : `${Math.round(s / 3600)} hours ago`
html`${vp == null
  ? html`<a class="live" href="#how-it-works"><span class="dot"></span>Saving bus locations every 20 seconds</a>`
  : vp.last_ok_age_s < 120
    ? html`<a class="live ok" href="#how-it-works"><span class="dot"></span>Saving now · last update ${ago(vp.last_ok_age_s)}</a>`
    : html`<a class="live down" href="#how-it-works"><span class="dot"></span>Collector delayed · last update ${ago(vp.last_ok_age_s)}</a>`}`
```
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {csv, json, pct, lateness, plural, longDate, routeMap, routeSlug} from "./lib.js"
import {drawRouteMap} from "./map.js"
recent = json("data/ontime/recent.json")
quality = csv(d3, "data/quality/daily.csv")
q = quality.at(-1) ?? null
o = recent?.overall ?? null
period = recent == null ? "" : recent.days === 1
  ? `on ${longDate(recent.last_service_date)}`
  : `over the ${recent.days} days to ${longDate(recent.last_service_date)}`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`${o == null || o.observed === 0
  ? html`<p class="empty">The first numbers appear after the first full day is processed, shortly after midnight Pacific.</p>`
  : html`<div class="headline">
      <div class="big">${pct(o.on_time_share_of_observed)}</div>
      <div class="big-label">of bus departures we could see left on time ${period}.
        <span class="note">On time means no more than 1 minute early or 5 minutes late.
        The typical departure was ${lateness(o.deviation_s_median)}.</span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="stat-row">
      <div class="stat"><div class="label">Departures checked</div>
        <div class="value">${o.observed.toLocaleString("en-US")}</div>
        <div class="note">at the stops printed in the timetables</div></div>
      <div class="stat"><div class="label">Late departures</div>
        <div class="value">${pct(o.late_share_of_observed)}</div>
        <div class="note">more than 5 minutes behind schedule</div></div>
      ${q == null ? "" : html`<div class="stat"><div class="label">Trips that showed up in the tracking</div>
        <div class="value">${pct(q.trip_coverage)}</div>
        <div class="note">of ${q.scheduled_trips.toLocaleString("en-US")} scheduled trips on ${longDate(q.service_date instanceof Date ? q.service_date.toISOString().slice(0, 10) : q.service_date)}</div></div>`}
    </div>`}`
```

## Every route at a glance

Each line is a bus route, colored by how often its buses left on time. Tap a
route to see it stop by stop.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css">`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
L = require("leaflet@1.9.4")
mapData = routeMap(recent?.timepoints)
homeMap = mapData == null ? null : drawRouteMap(L, mapData, recent, {
  height: width < 640 ? 420 : 580,
  onSelect: id => {
    const r = mapData.routes.find(r => r.route_id === id);
    location.href = `routes.html#${routeSlug(r, id)}`;
  },
})
html`${homeMap == null ? html`<p class="empty">The route map appears after the first day is processed.</p>` : homeMap.node}`
```

::: {.how-steps}
1. **The bus.** GPS on board reports where it is.
2. **The live feed.** Island Transit publishes those reports for trip apps;
   each update replaces the last one.
3. **Our collector.** Saves every update, every 20 seconds, day and night.
4. **Nightly checks.** Work out when buses left each stop and grade the
   tracking data.
5. **You.** This site's charts and map, plus every file to download.
:::
:::

The feed never says "the bus left the stop." It only says where the bus is.
So each night the saved locations are connected along the route to find the
moment each bus passed each stop, and that moment is compared with the
printed timetable. The same saved data also shows how often the tracking
itself fails: buses that never appear, gaps, stale locations, and arrival
predictions that miss.

## Why this exists

Live bus data disappears the moment it is replaced, and Island Transit does
not publish on-time figures. Keeping every update makes questions like "Was
route 60 late last week?" or "Does the tracking fail more at rush hour?"
answerable, by anyone, with the code to check the answer.

[Collecting since November 19, 2026. Not affiliated with Island Transit; the
figures are this project's own, calculated from Island Transit's public
data.]{.note}
